subject: Workplace Skills
title: Groupthink and Bad Decisions
description: One-minute skill: Groupthink and Bad Decisions.

hook.text: NASA engineers knew the Challenger O-rings were risky in cold weather. No one spoke up against the launch decision.

buildup.text: Groupthink occurs when the desire for consensus overrides realistic evaluation of alternatives and risks.

discovery.text: Warning signs: illusion of invulnerability, self-censorship, pressure on dissenters, and belief in group morality.

twist.text: High-trust teams are actually more vulnerable to groupthink. Comfort makes people less willing to rock the boat.

climax.text: Appoint a devil's advocate for major decisions. Reward the person who finds the flaw everyone else missed.

punchline.text: Welcome the dissenter. They might save the mission.

quiz.question: Why are high-trust teams vulnerable to groupthink?
options: They communicate less frequently than low-trust teams
Comfort and trust make people reluctant to voice dissent
They lack the skills for independent critical thinking
